title: Optimal Surplus Management for Insurers under Stochastic Interest Rates and Jump-Driven Liabilities
summary: This paper investigates the optimal surplus management problem of an insurance company operating in a financial market with stochastic interest rates and jump-driven liabilities. The insurer dynamically allocates its surplus between a risky stock and a risk-free zero-coupon bond while facing insurance claims modeled by a compound Poisson process with exponentially distributed claim sizes. The short term interest rate follows a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) process, which captures mean-reverting dynamics commonly observed in term structure models.
